Who Was Theodore McCarrick?

ARCHBISHOP. CARDINAL. PREDATOR. THE WOLF.
THE RISE

Theodore Edgar McCarrick was ordained a priest of the Archdiocese of New York in 1958. He rose with unusual speed through the American Catholic hierarchy—Bishop of Metuchen in 1981, Archbishop of Newark in 1986, Archbishop of Washington in 2000, Cardinal in 2001.

He was celebrated as a diplomatic powerhouse. He advised presidents. He raised hundreds of millions of dollars for the Church. He was photographed with popes. He was, by every visible measure, one of the most powerful Catholics in America.

He was also, throughout all of it, a serial predator of seminarians, young men, and children.

THE METHOD

McCarrick maintained a beach house in Sea Girt, New Jersey. He invited seminarians and young priests for weekends. He shared beds. He called it mentorship. His victims called it something else. Many of them did not speak publicly for decades—because he was their bishop, their career, their God's representative on earth.

The abuse was not a secret. It was an open secret—known to his secretaries, known to his chancery, known to Rome. Complaints were filed. Settlements were paid. He was promoted anyway.

In 2018, the Vatican stripped him of his cardinalate. In 2019, he became the first cardinal in modern history to be laicized—reduced to the lay state—by Pope Francis. He is the only cardinal in modern history to be so punished.

WHAT HE LEFT BEHIND

McCarrick is dead. He died February 16, 2025, at age 94, at a Franciscan friary in Victoria, Kansas — laicized, disgraced, convicted, never imprisoned. He died before the machine he built was dismantled. The machine is still running.

One of the men named in the 2019 Latham Report—Msgr. Joseph Reilly, who served as McCarrick's personal secretary and admitted to visiting the Sea Girt beach house—is currently the President of Seton Hall University. He was elected to that position in 2024. He is still in office.
